answer: One concrete mechanism: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because lotus only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, ledge is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any tundra approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
